questions.question: 1. What is the fundamental concept of frequency reuse in a cellular system?

answers.a: Assigning a unique frequency to every user in the network.
answers.b: Using the same set of frequencies in different cells that are geographically separated.
answers.c: Using different frequencies for voice calls and data transmission.
answers.d: Allowing two adjacent cells to share the exact same frequency set.

answers.a: Cells that are immediately next to each other.
answers.b: Cells that use two different, non-overlapping frequency bands.
answers.c: Cells that belong to a different network operator.
answers.d: Cells that are assigned the same set of frequencies.

4. What is the main advantage of using the frequency reuse technique?

answers.a: It increases the overall capacity of the network.
answers.b: It completely eliminates all forms of interference.
answers.c: It simplifies the hardware design of a mobile phone.
answers.d: It increases the signal strength in every cell.

questions.question: 5. In frequency reuse, what does a 'cluster' represent?

answers.a: A group of users connected to the same cell tower.
answers.b: A group of cells in which the entire available frequency spectrum is used exactly once.
answers.c: All the cells that are experiencing interference at the same time.
answers.d: A single, large cell designed to cover a wide rural area.

answers.a: The distance between a mobile phone and the nearest cell tower.
answers.b: The radius of a single cell.
answers.c: The distance between the centers of the two nearest co-channel cells.
answers.d: The distance between two adjacent cells.

questions.question: 7. What is the main consequence of using a **small** cluster size?

answers.a: The system capacity decreases, but co-channel interference also decreases.
answers.b: The system capacity increases, but co-channel interference also increases.
answers.c: The frequency reuse distance becomes larger.
answers.d: Both system capacity and co-channel interference decrease.

questions.question: 8. What is the main consequence of using a **large** cluster size?

answers.a: Co-channel interference is reduced, but the total system capacity is also reduced.
answers.b: Co-channel interference is increased, but the total system capacity is also increased.
answers.c: The physical size of each cell must be increased.
answers.d: Both co-channel interference and system capacity increase.

questions.question: 9. How can co-channel interference be reduced?

answers.a: By moving the co-channel cells closer to each other.
answers.d: By making all cells use the same set of frequencies.

questions.question: 10. For good call quality, what must be true about the signal-to-interference ratio?

answers.a: The ratio must be as low as possible.
answers.b: The desired signal power should be much higher than the interference power.
answers.c: The desired signal power should be equal to the interference power.
answers.d: The ratio is not related to call quality.
